Article Title: Sam Pitroda, PM Modi display rare public bonhomie
Article Text:
Sam Pitroda, PM Modi display rare public bonhomie

NEW DELHI: Congress's overseas wing head, Sam Pitroda, is a vocal critic of PM Narendra Modi and the key organiser of Rahul Gandhi 's overseas outreach events.But the festive season brought out of him rare words of praise for Modi, who in turn extended his Diwali greetings to the fellow Gujarati.Modi said, "Happy Diwali and Nutan Varsh Abhinandan to you Sam Bhai and to Anjana Ben. Praying for a joyful and healthy year ahead. Jai Jagannath!"In remarks to a news agency, Pitroda had called Modi a "Gujarati friend" whom he respects as a person."My wife and I have met him. He has been very warm, kind, loving and caring at a personal level. Of course, he is a good orator and hard-working, and we get along well. We have no personal issues. I have nothing against Mr Modi as a Gujarati leader, friend or well-wisher. He has been very warm towards me, and I appreciate that. Similarly, I have been to his house in Gujarat several times," he said.Modi's greetings took even some BJP supporters by surprise. One said on X if he could wish Pitroda, he could wish him as well. Sure enough, Modi posted his Diwali greetings to him.
Article Summary: Congress's overseas wing head, Sam Pitroda, is a vocal critic of PM Narendra Modi. But the festive season brought out of him rare words of praise for Modi. Modi in turn extended his Diwali greetings to the fellow Gujarati.

Article Title: 'India showed world yoga': PM Modi praises HV Sheshadri at Bengaluru event
Article Text:
PM Modi in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday praised writer and RSS leader HV Sheshadri for his contribution to nation-building, saying he dedicated his life to preparing "dedicated, capable, and disciplined citizens".Speaking at the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram at S-VYASA University in Bengaluru, PM also highlighted India's efforts to take its cultural heritage, traditional knowledge and scientific achievements to the global stage."Friends, along with the grand jubilee of Prashanti Kuttrem, this year we are celebrating the birth centenary of the revered H.V. Sheshadri. I pay my respectful homage. Sheshadri dedicated his entire life to furthering the mission of nation-building through the creation of the H.V. Seshadri Institute," PM Modi said."He knew that to take the country to the pinnacle of success it would require dedicated, capable, and disciplined citizens. Sheshadri ji devoted himself to preparing such individuals," PM Modi added.The Prime Minister also spoke about India's spiritual legacy, recalling the contribution of Swami Vivekananda in awakening the country's spiritual consciousness and introducing yoga to its youth."When the country was shackled by the chains of slavery, millions of freedom fighters were fighting for independence on one side... while on the other, there were national sages like Swami Vivekananda, who awakened India's spiritual consciousness. Showed India's youth the path of yoga. Over the past 12 years, India has confidently presented its culture, its identity, and its knowledge and science to the world. This is why the whole world now celebrates International Day of Yoga at India's initiative. Yoga asanas have also been recognized as a competitive sport in India.Events such as Khelo India and the National Games have also created new opportunities for yoga asanas. These changes are very important for India. They have also opened up opportunities for people involved. We have encouraged research related to Ayurveda and Ayurveda-based patents, and today we are seeing the results of that too. Exports of AYUSH and herbal products from India are steadily increasing," the PM said.The Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram and the birth centenary of HV Sheshadri was organised by the S-VYASA Registered Society in memory of the writer. RSS Sarkaryavah (General Secretary) Dattatreya Hosabale was the distinguished guest at the event.PM was welcomed on his arrival by Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar. Governor Sudha Yadav was also present.The Prime Minister is also scheduled to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru.Among the projects is the elevated section of Namma Metro's Pink Line, which will take the city's operational metro network beyond the 100-km mark for the first time.The corridor connecting Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere covers six stations — Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIMB (Bilekahalli-IIMB), JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi praised writer and RSS leader HV Sheshadri for his contribution to nation-building. PM also highlighted India's efforts to take its cultural heritage, traditional knowledge and scientific achievements to the global stage. PM is scheduled to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday renewed his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a one-on-one public debate, claiming that the prime minister would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange.During an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram, the Congress MP was asked why he continued to insist on a public debate when the BJP had said the discussion could take place in Parliament.The leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha said he was not allowed to speak freely in the House and alleged that his microphone had been switched off."You did not let me talk on the farm bills, vote chori, SIR, China, on (Gen) Naravane's book, Epstein. I want a one-on-one debate. I don't want a debate entailing long speeches," he said.The Raebareli MP proposed a direct exchange in which both leaders could make allegations against each other, rather than deliver lengthy speeches."I want that Narendra Modi makes allegations against me and I do the same to him. He can come; there will be a table, on one side there will be Narendra Modi ji and on the other side, it would be me," he said.He added that he would have no objection if Adani Group chairperson Gautam Adani or Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat was appointed to judge the debate."But I guarantee that the prime minister will not remain the PM after a one-on-one debate with me," Rahul said.He also alleged that PM Modi is anti-national and is controlled by foreign powers.Responding to a question regarding proof of such foreign aid allegations, he said, “The proof is here. It's in this phone. The Prime Minister knows it because he taps my phone. The moment he comes for the debate, one-on-one debate, everybody will know who's controlled by foreign powers, who's an anti-national, since when he's been an anti-national, and lots of other details that I know and I wrote on my phone.”The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate. He had earlier claimed that it would take him just five minutes to establish that the prime minister was a "traitor".In a series of posts and videos shared on X last week, Rahul also challenged PM Modi to debate allegations concerning foreign influence, national security and who was anti-national.In one video, he said 24 hours had passed since he first issued the challenge and urged the prime minister to choose any venue. He proposed that the discussion take place in front of the media and the country's youth, with both leaders seated across a table and PM Modi choosing the moderator or judge. Rahul had suggested Bhagwat for the role.In another post, former Congress president renewed the challenge while responding to PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks. Addressing CRPF personnel who had attended the prime minister's Diwali event in Bastar, he claimed their expressions suggested they did not agree with PM Modi's comments."Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals," Gandhi wrote.He also said the debate should address who was anti-national and who was controlled by foreign forces.BJP leaders have scoffed at Rahul's repeated calls for a debate, alleging that he has avoided discussions in Parliament.Union home minister Amit Shah has challenged Rahul to debate him in Parliament, asking him to bring his allegations and arguments to the House instead of taking political debate to the streets."If you (Rahul Gandhi) wish to engage in a responsible discussion—if your concerns hold truth, substance, and logic—then come and discuss them inside Parliament. Let’s face each other head-on! But you won’t be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away," Shah said at a rally in Karnal, Haryana.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has also said that Parliament already provides a platform for such an exchange and urged the Congress MP to show "some seriousness and responsibility" in his role as the leader of the opposition.Rahul's latest remarks come amid the continuing political exchange between the Congress and the BJP over his allegations against Modi and the prime minister's criticism of the opposition.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi renews his challenge to PM Modi for a one-on-one public debate. He claims PM Modi would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange. The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate.

Article Title: Some people think democracy is in their pockets, says PM Modi
Article Text:
Some people think democracy is in their pockets, says PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi Thursday launched a sharp attack on Congress and took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi without naming him, saying some people carry the Constitution in their pockets and think the country's Constitution and democracy are indeed in their pockets.Addressing the India Today Group's Bharat Kisan Conclave, Modi said these people continue to display what he described as an "undue sense of entitlement" despite no longer being in govt. "Even when they are not in office, they behave this way. It is a strange kind of intoxication of power," he said.During his speech, he recalled an incident from his tenure as Gujarat CM, alleging the then central govt had pressured researchers to seek its approval before publishing economic rankings.The PM said that Gujarat had secured the number one position in an economic performance list published by an organisation named after a former PM, with the ranking based on research conducted by some of the country's leading economists."The people in office in Delhi could not accept Gujarat being honoured. They actually instructed the researchers that things would not work this way and that, before publishing any report, they would have to seek our approval," said the PM.Speaking on agriculture, the PM stressed that agricultural development, smarter farming and farmer empowerment are key to building a 'Viksit Bharat'.He underlined that India offers growing opportunities in everything from agri-engineering to agri-startups, and said the focus of his govt is on empowering farmers to become agricultural entrepreneurs.Citing a World Bank study, he claimed nearly 50 crore people had come out of poverty over the past 12 to 13 years and highlighted that small farmers and agricultural labourers were among them, while rural areas had witnessed a significant decline in poverty.Earlier in the day, Modi said that India will achieve its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 as the mindset has changed and targets set by govt, which appeared impossible, have been met."When a deadline is set, priorities change, the way of working changes and the speed changes too. And the achievements with which India is moving forward today, achieving the goal of a developed India is not impossible. Just think what India has achieved in the past few years," Modi said during a post-Diwali meeting with journalists at BJP headquarters."The 2047 deadline doesn't mean that we have to wait until then. Remember the freedom movement; the goal of 'Poorna Swaraj' was not going to be achieved in a year or two. But smaller goals were set. They were fulfilled and then belief grew in people that freedom would surely come and the whole country stood up with this resolve.""The same belief in the country will take us to the goal of a developed India. We will move forward by achieving many small and large goals..." the PM said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi said some people carry the Constitution in their pockets. He said these people display an "undue sense of entitlement" despite no longer being in govt. Modi said that India will achieve its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Article Title: Uttar Pradesh elections 2027: Who will Owaisi-Azad alliance hurt most? Explained in 5 charts

NEW DELHI: Asaduddin Owaisi wanted a place in the INDIA bloc's fight against the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Bihar rebuke and several olive branches later, he warned four months ago: "I have said this before, and I am saying it again: the Majlis does not want the BJP to form the government again in Uttar Pradesh. I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again."But the Samajwadi Party and the Congress, who are yet to formalise their own seat-sharing plan, did not pay heed to him.Owaisi on Thursday joined hands with Chandrashekhar Azad to build an alternative political platform in Uttar Pradesh. This time, along with challenging the BJP, the AIMIM chief declared: "If we have to die for the cause of people, it's a good deal for us; Akhilesh Yadav won't be CM, engaged in politics of entitlement."The newly-formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha, with Azad as its chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly elections, is seeking to mobilise Dalits, Muslims and backward communities under a common political platform.And the proposition is significant. Muslims account for an estimated 19 per cent of UP's electorate, Dalits 21 per cent and OBCs around 41 per cent. The two communities at the heart of the new alliance, Muslims and Dalits, together constitute around 40 per cent of the electorate.But demographic arithmetic obviously does not automatically translate into votes.The Uttar Pradesh contest is already too crowded with the BJP, Samajwadi Party, BSP, Congress and even smaller caste-based parties within the NDA. Chirag Paswan's Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), too, is looking to expand its presence in UP ahead of the elections.So how will this new Owaisi-Azad alliance fit into the play?But first, let's rewind a bit.In Bihar, ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, Owaisi offered to contest just six seats as part of the RJD-led INDIA bloc. In September 2025, he had said that AIMIM's Bihar president Akhtarul Iman had written three letters, two to Lalu Prasad Yadav and one to Tejashwi Yadav, seeking an alliance."We are ready to take six seats. You don't even have to give us a ministry if you come to power. Just set up a Seemanchal development board. What more can we do?" Owaisi had said.The RJD-Congress-led Mahagathbandhan did not accommodate AIMIM despite Owaisi's offer to contest just six seats. The decision came despite AIMIM's five-seat breakthrough in the 2020 Bihar assembly elections, when it won all its seats in Seemanchal. Four of those five MLAs later defected to the RJD in 2022.But the party demonstrated that its support base had survived the defections. Contesting independently in 28 constituencies in 2025, AIMIM won five seats again, retaining all five constituencies it had won in 2020. Its performance came as a setback to the Mahagathbandhan in Seemanchal, where the NDA won 14 of the region's 24 seats, while the Congress and RJD managed five between them.Cut to one year later, Owaisi once again expressed his willingness to work with Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh, that too repeatedly. The SP, however, dismissed his public overtures as "public posturing", arguing that electoral alliances were not negotiated through public statements.The SP's reluctance to accommodate AIMIM has now resulted in Owaisi building a separate front with Azad.In an interview with The TOI ahead of the alliance announcement, Owaisi said the two parties were already "shortlisting the seats and discussing who will contest from where". He also said the alliance would remain open to other parties and individuals.Now here's how the Owaisi-Azad alliance may make the parties feel its impact in upcoming elections:The SP, led by Akhilesh Yadav, may have the most immediate reason to worry. Its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) strategy seeks to consolidate backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broad electoral coalition against the BJP.The Owaisi-Azad alliance is also attempting to mobilise precisely these constituencies, but outside the INDIA bloc opposition framework.The Muslim vote is the most immediate point of vulnerability for Akhilesh. Muslims account for approximately 19 per cent of UP's population and have overwhelmingly backed the SP in recent elections as the principal party challenging the BJP.The constituency-level data shows that there are 143 assembly seats where Muslims have a significant electoral presence: 70 seats where their population share is estimated at 20-30 per cent and another 73 where it exceeds 30 per cent.The concentration is particularly important in Rohilkhand and the Upper Doab. Constituencies such as Rampur Nagar, Chamrauwa, Moradabad Rural, Kundarki, Behat, Amroha, Sambhal, Suar, Moradabad Nagar and Najibabad have estimated Muslim population or voter shares ranging from around 45 per cent to over 60 per cent.This gives AIMIM a potential electoral geography.The analysis of 59 Muslim-dominated constituencies in the 2022 assembly elections offers another indication of the stakes. The SP won 34 seats against the BJP's 22, but the BJP's vote share was marginally higher at 39.3 per cent, against the SP's 39.1 per cent.Owaisi has repeatedly questioned why Muslim voters should continue supporting parties that seek their votes but do not offer them an adequate share in political representation.This new alliance with Azad may give Owaisi a stronger political argument. Instead of merely seeking a share of the Muslim vote, he can now pitch a broader Dalit-Muslim coalition, with Azad bringing a Dalit support base and the credibility of having won the Nagina Lok Sabha seat in 2024. This could help the alliance present itself as an alternative social and political formation, rather than just another party seeking to divide the opposition's Muslim vote.For Akhilesh, even a limited erosion of Muslim support could matter in closely contested constituencies.If Owaisi's immediate target is the SP's Muslim support base, Azad's political ambition could put pressure on the BSP and Mayawati.Dalits account for approximately 21 per cent of UP's electorate, but they are not a homogeneous political constituency.While Jatavs have remained the BSP's traditional support base, the BJP has steadily expanded its appeal among non-Jatav Dalit communities, including Pasis, who account for an estimated 4 per cent of the electorate. Through targeted outreach, welfare politics and the mobilisation of smaller caste groups, the BJP has drawn sections of these communities into its broader social coalition. This has further eroded the BSP's ability to command Dalit votes as a consolidated bloc.The BSP's vote share fell from 22.23 per cent in the 2017 assembly elections to 12.88 per cent in 2022. Its seat tally collapsed from 19 to just one. Azad's entry into the alliance could now open another front in this contest for Dalit support.Azad first emerged as a prominent Dalit voice through the Bhim Army, the organisation he co-founded in 2015 to fight caste discrimination and work for Dalit rights, particularly through education and grassroots mobilisation. His activism, often marked by confrontations with the authorities over caste-related violence, helped him build a following among Dalit youth in western Uttar Pradesh.His victory from Nagina in the 2024 Lok Sabha election gave him a parliamentary platform and established him as an electoral force, taking him beyond his earlier identity as a Dalit rights activist.For Mayawati, the challenge is not simply that Azad is emerging as a younger Dalit leader. It is that he is attempting to combine Dalit political assertion with Muslim representation, a combination that could appeal to voters looking for a new social justice platform.However, replacing Mayawati is no easy task. The BSP has a decades-old organisational network and a political identity built around Kanshi Ram's Bahujan movement.Azad will have to demonstrate that his appeal extends beyond Nagina and sections of the Jatav community. The bigger test will be whether he can attract non-Jatav Dalits, particularly in central and eastern UP, where the BJP has consolidated support among several smaller caste groups.For the BJP, the alliance is both good and bad news.On one hand, if Owaisi draws Muslim votes away from the SP and Azad takes away some Dalit support from the BSP and SP, the anti-BJP vote could become fragmented. This could work in the BJP's favour.The BJP won 255 seats in the 2022 assembly elections with 41.29 per cent of the vote. The SP secured 111 seats with 32.06 per cent.On the other hand, the alliance's attempt to mobilise non-Jatav Dalits and backward communities could challenge the BJP's own social coalition.The BJP's electoral strategy in UP has relied heavily on consolidating non-Yadav OBCs, who account for an estimated 33 per cent of the electorate, and non-Jatav Dalits.The BJP has successfully brought sections of these communities into its fold since 2014 through political representation, welfare outreach and alliances with smaller caste-based parties. These include Apna Dal (Sonelal), which has influence among Kurmis; the SBSP, led by Om Prakash Rajbhar, which draws support from Rajbhars; and the NISHAD Party, which represents riverine communities such as Nishads, Mallahs and Kewats. Together, these parties have helped the BJP build a broader non-Yadav OBC coalition across Uttar Pradesh, particularly in eastern UP.Azad's attempt to mobilise marginalised communities could put this support base under pressure. However, the alliance will have to demonstrate that it can translate its social justice pitch into votes across constituencies.The BJP, under CM Yogi Adityanath, also has an established organisational network and a much larger electoral footprint than either AIMIM or the Azad Samaj Party.For the ruling party, the bigger advantage could come if the new alliance weakens the SP's ability to consolidate anti-incumbency votes.The Congress could also face a challenge, although its direct electoral vulnerability seems less clear.The party has been trying to rebuild its presence in Uttar Pradesh through its alliance with the SP and the broader INDIA bloc.Its outreach to Dalits and minorities overlaps with the social constituencies that Owaisi and Azad are seeking to mobilise.The alliance could complicate Congress's attempt to expand its independent support base, particularly among Muslim voters who have increasingly backed the SP as the principal challenger to the BJP.The UP assembly contest has intensified with the entry of a new opposition front.Will Owaisi and Azad be able to translate their Dalit-Muslim political alliance into a viable electoral force in Uttar Pradesh? And can the two leaders build a support base strong enough to challenge established players and make the Samajik Parivartan Morcha a factor in the 2027 assembly elections? We will know in the coming months.
Article Summary: Owaisi declared Chandrashekhar Azad as the Samajik Parivartan Morcha's CM candidate. Azad said marginalised communities will use their votes to assert political power. Muslims account for 19 per cent of UP's electorate, Dalits 21 per cent and OBCs around 41 per cent.

NEW DELHI: Amid continuing incidents of violence in ethnic-strife-hit Manipur , govt sources Thursday expressed confidence that the assembly polls in the state will be held on schedule.The term of the Manipur assembly ends on March 13 next year, and the state is due to go to the polls alongside Goa, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh However, a long phase of ethnic violence, which has subsided but continues to persist sporadically, has left political circles wondering if the Manipur polls will be held on time."It will be held on time," a source said when asked.EC, which has been making preparations, put Manipur's electorate at 19.94 lakh in its draft rolls, signalling an expansion of the voter base by nearly 2% before assembly elections expected by March. The draft rolls, prepared after a special summary revision (SSR), added 33,737 electors to the rolls published following Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Sept.The 60 assembly constituencies of the state registered a rise in voter numbers, with women outnumbering men by 55,437. Saikot recorded the highest gain of more than 2,600 electors.The window for filing claims and objections will remain open until Dec 11. The final rolls will be published on Jan 4.
Article Summary: The term of the Manipur assembly ends on March 13 next year. The state is due to go to the polls alongside Goa, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. A long phase of ethnic violence has subsided but continues to persist sporadically.

Article Title: Kashmiri wazas stir Valley pot with 10 pm wazwan deadline, politics takes back seat
Article Text:
Kashmiri wazas stir Valley pot with 10 pm wazwan deadline, politics takes back seat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: At the end of the marriage season, wedding chefs, called wazas in Kashmir, have created a storm in the Valley by announcing that they will stop serving wazwan, the traditional multi-course Kashmiri meal, after 10 pm in an attempt to curb increasingly late-night wedding feasts. The decision is being widely debated on social media in Kashmir and politics, it appears, has taken a backseat for the moment.The dinner deadline will take effect from the next marriage season, which begins in May, according to All Kashmir Waza Association president Ghulam Nabi Baba. Under the new proposed arrangement, Baba said lunch wazwan would be served at 2 pm and dinner at around 10 pm. He said members who fail to follow the association’s rules would be removed.Baba said the decision was taken at an association meeting at Rajouri Kadal, in Srinagar’s old city, on Wednesday in response to the growing trend of delayed groom arrivals at wedding venues. Some grooms, he said, reach the bride’s home as late as 3 or 4 am, when they should be having a feast much before 10 pm.“From next season, starting in May, this will not be tolerated,” Baba told TOI. With the changing security situation in the Valley, late-night weddings have become the norm, but the wazas are not happy about it.They have their reasons. Baba said serving wazwan past midnight creates problems as younger people are reluctant to join the profession, presuming it more demanding, while labourers hired for the day are unwilling to work through the night after remaining on duty for long hours.Baba said the timing decision would be implemented through the association, which is 60 years old and has chefs from across the Valley as members. “Our association is registered and has at least 40,000 members,” he said. “We will introduce an agreement that the groom’s or bride’s family hiring us will have to sign,” he said.In South Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Waza said the delays were affecting the livelihoods of chefs and their ability to manage bookings. “The lack of fixed timings is affecting our business. We are unable to commit to dates due to delays. The delays are hitting everyone hard — customers and guests who come to enjoy the feast,” he said.The association’s announcement has prompted wider social media debate. “I have a request for the Waza Association. Please do not accept processed spices, cockscomb, garlic paste, colourants or powdered milk. Give us the original wazwan we once cherished and do not make more than seven dishes,” reads a post on Facebook.“Restricting the timing of wazwan functions and ensuring that they do not continue beyond reasonable hours is certainly a need of society… But there is another equally important issue: Who is monitoring the rates charged by wazas?” read another post.One social media post accusing them of experimenting with more mutton dishes and making a marriage feast a costly affair shows mutton dishes prepared in grenade and AK-47 shapes in response to Baba’s deadline statement. Baba said the association will encourage its members to follow the traditional seven-course meal.
Article Summary: All Kashmir Waza Association president Ghulam Nabi Baba said lunch wazwan would be served at 2 pm and dinner at around 10 pm. The decision was taken at an association meeting at Rajouri Kadal, in Srinagar’s old city. The dinner deadline will take effect from the next marriage season.

Article Title: After back-to-back failures, Isro successfully tests modified PSLV 3rd stage
Article Text:

BENGALURU: In an important step towards restoring the reliability of its workhorse Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), Isro Thursday said it successfully conducted a ground static test of the rocket’s modified third stage (PS3) at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) in Sriharikota.The test, conducted on Thursday, follows two consecutive PSLV mission failures in which anomalies were observed in the rocket’s third stage. Isro said it had comprehensively reviewed the stage’s design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures and quality checks before introducing modifications to strengthen the system.Isro said the modified PS3 solid motor incorporates improvements to its nozzle configuration and mechanical interfaces, along with additional redundancy in its sealing systems. The space agency has also revised procedures for accepting raw materials, assembling the motor and conducting non-destructive tests (NDT) during integration and transportation.The mechanical interfaces have also been strengthened, with redundancy introduced in the sealing systems. Isro said the adequacy of design margins had been verified and updated non-destructive testing procedures had been implemented at different stages of integration and transportation.The modifications follow setbacks involving PSLV-C61/EOS-09 in May 2025 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 in Jan 2026. Both missions encountered problems during the third stage, raising concerns about the reliability of a launch vehicle that has been central to India’s satellite launch programme.On May 18, 2025, PSLV-C61, carrying the 1,696-kg EOS-09 Earth observation satellite, lifted off from Sriharikota. While the first two stages performed normally, Isro detected a fall in chamber pressure during the third-stage burn, preventing the rocket from completing its mission. A national-level committee was subsequently constituted to investigate the failure and recommend corrective measures.The second setback came on Jan 12, 2026, when PSLV-C62, carrying the EOS-N1 Earth observation satellite and 15 co-passenger payloads, encountered an anomaly towards the end of its third stage. The vehicle experienced disturbances in its roll rates, followed by a deviation in its flight path, and could not place the satellites in their intended orbits.While both failures involved the third stage, the specific circumstances reported were different. The latest modifications, Isro said, followed a comprehensive review of the PS3 configuration and were aimed at improving its design margins and manufacturing and quality-control processes.The space agency said the performance of the modified solid motor and its subsystems would now be assessed through a detailed analysis of the test data. Further tests are planned based on the findings.The PSLV, a four-stage launch vehicle, has been a mainstay of India's space programme, undertaking missions ranging from Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission to Aditya-L1. Its return to dependable flight operations is important not only for Isro's own missions but also for India's commercial satellite launch commitments.
Article Summary: Isro conducted a ground static test of the rocket’s modified third stage (PS3) The test, conducted on Thursday, follows two consecutive PSLV mission failures in which anomalies were observed in the rocket's third stage. Isro said the modified PS3 solid motor incorporates improvements to its nozzle configuration and mechanical interfaces.

NEW DELHI: The government is planning to convene a special session of Parliament to secure the passage of a Constitution amendment bill linked to the implementation of women's reservation, PTI reported.According to the report, the BJP-led Centre is confident of securing 15 to 18 votes more than the 361 required to achieve a two-thirds majority and pass the proposed legislation. However, the dates and duration of the proposed special session remain unclear.The possibility of convening Parliament at short notice remains open, as the Monsoon Session, during which both Houses were adjourned sine die (indefinitely) on August 13, has yet to be prorogued. The session has now remained unprorogued for 91 days, surpassing the previous record of 87 days set in 2008.While an extended sitting of an existing session requires a minimum notice of two days, convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.The government's decision to keep the Monsoon Session unprorogued has consequently triggered speculation about the possibility of an extended sitting or a special session to consider the proposed amendment.The Constitution does not specify any timeframe within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die. Nor does keeping a session in continuation without formally proroguing it for an extended period, by itself, constitute any constitutional or procedural impropriety.The proposed constitutional amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies.The move follows the failure of a similar Constitution amendment bill to secure the required majority in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget Session on April 17.The government is proposing a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state to address concerns raised by southern states, as it seeks to implement the women's reservation law before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.A fresh draft, which builds on the earlier bill, is understood to propose retaining the existing proportion of seats among states based on the 1971 Census.However, this is among several proposals under consideration, and no final decision has been taken, according to government sources.
Article Summary: The Centre is reportedly confident of securing 15-18 more votes than the 361 required to achieve a two-thirds majority and pass the proposed legislation. US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Article Title: Matt Henry vs India: A familiar storyline awakens ghosts of the past
Article Text:
New Zealand's Matt Henry, left, bowls against India during a One Day International cricket match in Tauranga, New Zealand, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief Scores

MOUNT MAUNGANUI: Seagulls began circling the Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui in full force just as India were about to begin their run chase. Little did they know that they would soon be joined by flying ducks as Matt Henry ran through the visitors' top order, dismissing Rohit Sharma Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in the very first over of India's innings.Henry needed just six deliveries to awaken the ghosts of the 2019 World Cup semifinal, sending back three right-handers for ducks. The only consolation for India seven years ago was that their top three -- KL Rahul, Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli -- had at least managed to score one run each.Chasing 334, India lost Rohit off the first ball. Rohit closed his bat face a bit early and was squared up, Kohli was cleaned up by a sharp in-dipper that kept a tad low, and India's stand-in skipper Iyer had no response to a delivery that jagged back sharply after pitching. Using his magic length and dangerous wobble seam, Henry put India on the mat in the very first over. Spectators who had stepped out for a quick hydration and refuelling break were shocked when they looked at the scoreline on the giant screen, and some even started walking out with disappointment written all over their faces.They had come hoping to witness special knocks from Kohli and Rohit but would have to make peace with the long walks back to the dressing room.And before they could settle back into their respective chairs or on the grass banks, Iyer joined the duck parade. Matters could have been worse had Nick Kelly held on to a regulation catch offered by Axar Patel off the first delivery he faced. Seeing Henry breathe fire, Kyle Jamieson soon joined the hunting pack, getting rid of Ruturaj Gaikwad as India lost four wickets inside the first 10 overs.Henry was not done. He returned to the attack and struck immediately, ending Ishan Kishan's resistance with his very first delivery. Bowling from round the wicket, the New Zealand pacer got one to jag back sharply from a good length. Ishan moved forward to defend but left a gap between bat and pad. The inside edge ricocheted onto the leg-stump, clipping the bail and ending his innings. The 34-year-old completed his five-wicket haul, his fourth in ODIs, with another display of his trademark nagging line and length and a hint of inward movement. Henry got the ball to nip back in sharply. Kuldeep Yadav was late in getting forward, allowing the delivery to beat his inside edge and defence before crashing into the top of the off-stump.Matt Henry finished with his career-best figures of 6/27 as New Zealand hammered India by 244 runs.This was the third time India had suffered this unwanted feat in ODIs since 2018, and all three instances featured the common wreaker-in-chief: Henry. The fast bowler picked up two wickets when India lost four in Wellington in 2019, three during the World Cup semifinal at Old Trafford the same year, and continued with his habit at the Bay Oval.The pitch didn't change drastically when twilight set in, but the evening chill injected just enough life into the surface, which had looked very comfortable for batting during New Zealand's innings. More than the surface, Henry found the right spot from the word go and stuck to it with his wobble seam. The two turned out to be a deadly combination, yet again, and made India join the list of several unwanted firsts.This was only the second time both Kohli and Rohit had registered ducks in an ODI and the first instance in which India lost three wickets without adding anything to the scoreboard. It had happened only four times earlier in the history of one-day cricket.India would hope to forget those six deliveries like a horror dream and bounce back strongly when they return to the same venue for the fixture that will decide the series."45 minutes of bad cricket (in Kohli's words)" against an attack featuring the usual suspect, Henry, had "cost" India the semifinal back in 2019. This time, it took Henry only a few minutes to stamp his authority in a series he had missed due to a freak injury. The eventful over nicely sets up the final match and the Test series that follows. Henry vs India remains a very interesting storyline.New Zealand: 333 all out in 50 overs (Will Young 125, Finn Allen 41; Axar Patel 2/39, Auqib Nabi 2/59, Gurnoor Brar 2/69)India: 89 all out in 26.4 overs (Ishan Kishan 27; Matt Henry 6/27, Matthew Fisher 3/31)
Article Summary: Matt Henry takes career-best figures of 6/27 as New Zealand beat India by 244 runs. Henry dismisses Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in the first over of India's innings. India lost four wickets inside the first 10 overs of their innings.

A reunion between Tyreek Hill and the Kansas City Chiefs might sound exciting to fans who remember his explosive partnership with Patrick Mahomes . But bringing the wide receiver back to Arrowhead could create problems that go far beyond football. Hill's serious knee injury, questions about his long-term fitness and a controversial off-field history have made the possibility difficult to ignore. With Kansas City looking for more firepower in its receiving group, the temptation to bring back a familiar superstar may exist. However, the Chiefs could have compelling reasons to look elsewhere.Hill's familiarity with Andy Reid's offensive system makes him an attractive name whenever Kansas City's receiving needs come into discussion. He spent six seasons with the Chiefs, building a dangerous connection with Mahomes before joining the Miami Dolphins in 2022.His speed and ability to turn short passes into explosive plays helped make him one of the NFL 's most feared receivers. Yet his current physical condition raises serious questions about whether he could deliver the same impact.Hill suffered a devastating knee injury last September, involving torn cruciate ligaments and a dislocated kneecap.Such an injury can demand a long and difficult recovery, particularly for a player whose biggest strength depends on acceleration, speed and sudden changes of direction.Reports of lingering muscle weakness have added to concerns about his progress. At 32, Hill would also face the challenge of returning to elite form after major surgery.For the Chiefs, this would be more than a familiar player returning to a familiar offence. It would be a significant investment in a receiver whose ability to regain his previous level remains uncertain.The football concerns are only part of the problem. Hill's history away from the field could make a reunion an even more difficult decision for Kansas City.Hill pleaded guilty to domestic abuse by strangulation in 2015 involving his then-pregnant partner. More recently, a civil jury found him liable on multiple counts of assault in a separate case. These matters have continued to draw scrutiny around his public image and professional career.Any attempt to bring him back would therefore invite questions about the standards the Chiefs want to uphold. The franchise would have to consider how such a move could affect its relationship with supporters, its locker room culture and its wider reputation.Kansas City has championship ambitions, and Hill's experience could offer an immediate offensive boost if he returns to full fitness. But talent alone does not guarantee a successful signing.The Chiefs must weigh the potential football benefits against the medical uncertainty and wider concerns surrounding the receiver. With other options available in the market, pursuing a reunion could carry risks that outweigh the rewards.For now, speculation does not mean Kansas City has made an offer or begun negotiations. A reunion remains uncertain, and the Chiefs may decide that moving forward without their former star is the smarter choice.

Article Title: 6/24 on debut! Mahli Beardman rips through England as Australia take 1-0 lead

Debutant Mahli Beardman produced a sensational performance with the ball, claiming 6/24 to power Australia to a comfortable seven-wicket victory over England in the first ODI in Perth on Friday.England's batting line-up crumbled for just 131 in 33.4 overs after Australia elected to bowl. The hosts made light work of the chase, getting to 132/3 in 23.3 overs, with captain Mitch Marsh leading the charge through a blistering half-century.For Beardman, the dream debut was an occasion to cherish."It's just a great privilege and honour to be able to represent my country, and then to be able to go out and take a few wickets as well is just a cherry on top," he said.The contest, however, unfolded amid fresh tensions in Australian cricket following the publication of Usman Khawaja's autobiography this week. The former Australia batter claimed that knowledge of the 2018 ball-tampering episode in Cape Town was not limited to the players who were eventually punished.Current Test captain Pat Cummins strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as "100% wrong" during an hour-long press conference on Friday.David Warner, meanwhile, backed Khawaja's version while on television commentary. Warner himself had received a 12-month playing ban for his involvement in the scandal.On the field, Australia's fast bowlers made early inroads on a lively Perth Stadium surface. Spencer Johnson (3/42) and Xavier Bartlett (1/46) accounted for openers Ben Duckett, who scored nine, and Tom Banton, who managed 25.Beardman then took centre stage, dismantling England's middle and lower order with a superb display of seam bowling. The Western Australia pacer consistently hit the right lengths and extracted movement off the pitch, making life difficult for the visitors.Wicketkeeper Josh Inglis held catches to dismiss England captain Harry Brook for one, Joe Root for 17 and Jordan Cox for two, all falling to the 21-year-old right-arm quick.Sam Curran and Liam Dawson departed without troubling the scorers as Beardman became the first Australian since Tony Dodemaide in 1988 to claim five wickets on ODI debut.He was not finished yet. Beardman completed his six-wicket haul by having Jofra Archer caught at gully for 11. Gus Atkinson, England's highest scorer with an unbeaten 29, was left stranded as the innings folded.England briefly threatened to make the chase interesting when Atkinson bowled Travis Head for a golden duck in the second over. However, Marsh quickly took control, smashing four sixes on his way to a rapid fifty before Jamie Overton (1/35) dismissed him in the deep.Archer then removed Cooper Connolly for 27, but England had little left to offer. Matt Renshaw joined Inglis at the crease, and the pair completed the chase without further damage.The victory gives Australia a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series. The second match will be played in Adelaide on Sunday, with the final game scheduled in Hobart on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Australia beat England by seven wickets in first ODI in Perth. Mahli Beardman takes six wickets on his ODI debut for Australia. Mitch Marsh hits blistering half-century for hosts. Victory gives Australia a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.

Jeremy Cowdrey, son of former England cricket captain Colin Cowdrey , has won a costly legal battle with his neighbour after a dispute over a strip of land disrupted the sale of his £3.85 million country home in Kent. The disagreement, which began when Vanessa Gibson acquired land containing part of his private tennis court, escalated into a court case involving allegations of harassment, malicious falsehood and attempts to extract money. A judge ruled in Cowdrey’s favour, awarding him compensation and ordering Gibson to pay a substantial contribution towards his legal costs. The court dispute centred on a narrow strip of land that Cowdrey claimed was essential to the property and its planned sale.The dispute centred on Crowbourne Farm, a substantial country property in Goudhurst, Kent, bought by Jeremy Cowdrey in early 2022. As reported by The Independent in February 2025, the Grade II-listed farmhouse sits within more than 10 acres and includes a guest cottage, studio, barn, workshop, wine cellar, stables, woodland and two lakes, alongside a tennis court.Cowdrey’s disagreement with Vanessa Gibson, who lives in a nearby barn conversion, began after she bought a strip of land that included part of his tennis court.Gibson argued that the court extended onto land she owned, creating a boundary dispute between the neighbours.The Independent reported that Cowdrey eventually agreed to fence off the disputed section and relinquish any claim to it. The arrangement was intended to settle the disagreement, but the relationship between the two neighbours deteriorated further as Cowdrey attempted to sell the property.Cowdrey put Crowbourne Farm on the market in June 2023, initially advertising it for more than £3.25 million. According to The Independent, he claimed that several prospective buyers had been discouraged by Gibson’s correspondence and that he had agreed a £3.85 million sale with a couple before they withdrew.His legal team alleged that Gibson continued to present the boundary issue as unresolved, despite the earlier agreement. They also accused her of raising concerns about restrictive covenants, flooding and the property’s utility connections.The Standard reported that Cowdrey believed his neighbour was making allegations in an attempt to extract money from him while he was trying to sell the estate. At a preliminary hearing, his barrister argued that the correspondence was designed to jeopardise the transaction and pressure him into paying her.Gibson disputed the allegations. She maintained that her concerns were legitimate and related to the land she owned, including flooding that affected both properties.The case proceeded to Central London County Court, where Judge Jane Evans-Gordon considered Cowdrey’s claims of malicious falsehood and harassment. The Independent reported in November 2025 that the judge found Gibson’s conduct had gone beyond protecting her own interests.The court decided that the earlier boundary dispute had been settled and that Gibson had attempted to conceal her intention to interfere with the sale. Her claims about continuing disagreements involving the tennis court, utility services and land covenants were found to be false.The judge said Gibson’s actions between March 2022 and June 2023 were motivated by an improper purpose, specifically causing financial loss by preventing Cowdrey from selling Crowbourne Farm unless he paid the amount she wanted.The judge considered that Gibson had concealed her purchase of the strip of land until she could use ownership to seek significant payment. While she was entitled to protect her interests, the court found that her conduct had crossed the line into a form of blackmail or maliciousness.Cowdrey had sought damages after the agreed £3.85 million sale collapsed. He argued that the property would have been worth around £3.7 million without Gibson’s allegations and claimed the difference between that figure and the failed sale price.Judge Evans-Gordon awarded him £150,000, together with interest, for the financial loss associated with the failed transaction. She also gave £9,000 in damages for the oppressive and unreasonable harassment he had experienced. The total compensation came to approximately £159,000 before interest.The financial consequences grew further when the parties returned to court over legal costs. The Independent reported in November 2025 that Gibson had been ordered to pay £360,000 towards Cowdrey’s legal expenses, including VAT, as an initial payment before the full costs were assessed.That amount was on top of the £159,000 compensation award. Together, the sums brought the immediate financial order to roughly £519,000, explaining reports that Cowdrey had won around £500,000 from his neighbour.Cowdrey’s barrister argued that Gibson should bear the substantial legal costs because of the way she had conducted the litigation. The judge ordered a significant portion of the costs to be assessed on an indemnity basis, a more demanding approach to costs recovery.Gibson told the court she did not have the money to pay the bill, according to The Independent.The November 2025 hearing also addressed how the neighbours would communicate in future. Gibson gave legally binding undertakings setting out how and when she could contact Cowdrey.Judge Evans-Gordon warned that breaching those commitments could amount to contempt of court. The Independent reported that she explained such a breach could carry a fine or imprisonment of up to 2 years.

India suffered their second-biggest defeat by runs in one-day internationals after New Zealand beat them by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday.Chasing 334 for victory, India were bowled out for just 89, with New Zealand pacer Matt Henry taking six wickets. Will Young led the hosts' batting effort with a century as they registered a dominant win.India still lead the five-match series 2-1. New Zealand cannot win the series but can level it by winning the final match at the same venue on Sunday. The third ODI was abandoned due to rain.India's 244-run defeat is now the second-biggest by runs in their ODI history. Their heaviest loss came against Sri Lanka, who beat them by 245 runs in Sharjah in 2000. The defeat against New Zealand is just one run short of that unwanted record.India's other biggest defeats include a 214-run loss to South Africa in Mumbai in 2015 and a 208-run defeat against Australia in Sydney in 2004.India's chase got off to a disastrous start as Henry struck three times in the opening over. He dismissed Rohit Sharma Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer to leave India reeling at 0/3.Ruturaj Gaikwad also fell soon after, leaving India in deep trouble.Ishan Kishan (27) and Axar Patel (21) then put together a 44-run partnership, while Naman Dhir added a quick 21.Their efforts helped India avoid an even bigger defeat. Henry returned to take three more wickets and finished with six as India were bowled out for their sixth-lowest total in ODIs.Earlier, Young produced a fine innings of 125 off 108 balls to give New Zealand a strong total. Both will also miss Sunday's final match as they prepare for the upcoming two-Test series against New Zealand, which begins on Wednesday.

Cristiano Ronaldo’s international career may have reached its conclusion, but his family’s association with Portugal has entered a new chapter. His eldest son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. , made his Under-17 debut in a 4-0 victory over Andorra in European Championship qualifying on Thursday, coming close to marking his first appearance with a goal after entering the match in the closing stages.The 16-year-old came off the bench in the 74th minute at Portugal’s national training centre in Oeiras, replacing Victor Bastianele with the hosts already holding a commanding advantage. Wearing the number 18 shirt, Ronaldo Jr. was given an opportunity to make his first appearance at Under-17 level after previously representing Portugal at Under-15 and Under-16 age groups.Portugal had established their four-goal lead before his introduction. Sporting CP forward Diego Farinha scored twice, while Kauã Miranda converted a penalty for the third goal and Braga's Rafael Cabral added another in the 60th minute. Filipe Ramos' side secured a comfortable opening victory in their qualifying campaign for the 2027 European Under-17 Championship.The occasion also attracted attention from Portugal's senior internationals. Vitinha, João Cancelo, João Félix and João Neves were among those watching from the sports complex in Oeiras as Ronaldo Jr. began his latest international assignment.Ronaldo Jr. nearly added a fifth goal in the closing stages, coming within inches of a memorable start to his Under-17 career. In the 88th minute, he connected with a cross from Diogo Djabi but sent his header narrowly wide of the goal.Although he could not find the net, the chance offered an early glimpse of his involvement at the new age level. He did not start the match and, unlike his father, did not wear Portugal's famous number seven shirt, instead appearing in number 18.The teenager arrived at the Under-17 level with an established record in Portugal's youth teams. His international journey began in May 2025, when he made his Under-15 debut wearing number seven at a tournament in Croatia. He subsequently represented the Under-16 side and helped Portugal win the Federation Cup in Turkey. Across his youth international appearances, he had scored five goals in 13 matches before making the step up.At club level, Ronaldo Jr. plays in the Al-Nassr academy in Saudi Arabia and has continued to attract attention with his performances, including a two-goal display against Al-Ahli earlier this season.The timing of the debut added another dimension to the occasion, coming just one week after his father announced his retirement from international football. Cristiano Ronaldo ended a 23-year Portugal career with a record 146 goals in 234 appearances, having represented the national team at the highest level since making his senior debut in 2003.Ronaldo Jr. now has the opportunity to establish his own place in Portugal's youth sides, with two further European Championship qualifiers scheduled during the current international window. Portugal are due to face Bulgaria on November 14 before meeting Serbia on November 17, with both matches taking place in Lisbon.The Andorra match was only his first appearance at Under-17 level, but the teenager will have further opportunities to gain experience as Portugal pursue qualification for the 2027 tournament.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. makes Portugal U17 debut against Andorra. Hours later, Norway said it would stop professional Russian and Belarusian sportspersons from competing on its soil.The decisions could affect major international sporting events scheduled in both countries.Finland has tightened rules for Russian citizens applying for short-term work visas, including those seeking to take part in professional sports.Under the new rules, "Russian citizens will only be allowed to work under a Schengen visa in tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests," the Finnish foreign ministry said in a statement.The restrictions will also apply to Russian athletes competing under a neutral flag. They will not be allowed to obtain visas to enter Finland."As long as Russia's war of aggression continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland," Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said in a statement."Their entry into the country would be a threat to Finland's international relations."The new rules will come into effect on November 16. Finland shares a 1,340-kilometre (830-mile) border with Russia.The country is scheduled to host the Figure Skating World Championships in Tampere in March 2027. The International Skating Union (ISU) said it was "studying" the possible impact of Finland's decision."The aim of the change is to prevent entries that Russia could use to spread messages supporting its war," Valtonen told reporters.Russia uses "sports as a tool for propaganda", she added.Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga welcomed Finland's move. In a post on X, he urged other European countries to "close the remaining loopholes, and strengthen coordinated pressure on Russia,".Norway announced its decision a few hours after Finland. Its government said the country already had strict visa rules for Russian and Belarusian citizens.However, recent "relaxations introduced by international sports federations" could allow more athletes and support staff from the two countries to travel to Norway for competitions.The new decision could prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes from competing even if they have been cleared by the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS).Norway is preparing to host the Cross-Country Skiing World Cup in Trondheim in December.The ISU said it believed athletes should not be held responsible for the actions of their governments. It said "that athletes should not be punished for the actions of the governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing".The governing body added that it was seeking "further clarifications" from the Finnish organisers.Finland's decision comes after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on October 30 opened the possibility of the Russian ice hockey team returning to the World Championships next year. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), which has banned Russia from competitions since its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, had opposed the CAS decision.Several countries, including Finland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic, have said they would refuse to play against Russia at the World Championships in Germany.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also said last week that Russia would not be allowed to compete at the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championships in Alberta. The Finnish city of Turku has announced that it will withdraw from hosting the 2027-28 edition of the tournament if Russia takes part.Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin last week praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for "taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles". He also criticised countries that are opposing Russia's return to international sport.
Article Summary: Finland says Russian athletes have 'no business' in country. Hours later, Norway also blocks Russian and Belarusian athletes. The decisions could affect major international sporting events scheduled in both countries. Finland shares a 1,340-kilometre (830-mile) border with Russia.

Article Title: 'No one threw their wicket away': Shreyas Iyer's blunt response after India's humiliating 244-run defeat against New Zealand
Article Text:
Shreyas Iyer

Iyer defends India's batting performance

Shreyas Iyer urges India to move on

India's stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer admitted that New Zealand's bowling made the difference after the visitors suffered a humiliating 244-run defeat in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday.Chasing 334, India were bowled out for just 89 in 28.4 overs, with Matt Henry producing a sensational six-wicket haul to dismantle the batting order. The defeat reduced India's lead in the five-match series to 2-1, with the third ODI having been washed out.Speaking after the match, Iyer acknowledged the impact of Henry's opening spell and credited the New Zealand pacer for consistently bowling in the right areas."We saw it, there was a huge difference in the first innings and the second innings in terms of wicket, but also credit where it's due, the way Henry bowled in the right areas right from ball one. I think that was sensational," Iyer said.India's batting collapse began in the opening over when Henry dismissed Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer, leaving the visitors reeling at 0/3. Iyer admitted that India had tried different bowling strategies during New Zealand's innings but struggled to contain the hosts. He also pointed to missed opportunities in the field, while acknowledging that the team expected to chase the target comfortably after watching New Zealand score 333."I think we tried almost everything in the first innings, the way they were playing on the rise. And we thought that the wicket was better to bat on considering they got 330 after that. Obviously a couple of dropped catches, but that definitely happens in a game," he said.The Indian captain also defended his batters, insisting that they were dismissed by quality deliveries rather than throwing their wickets away."But yeah, when we got into the dressing room, we thought that we would be cruising through the chase as well. But the way the ball was seaming in and out, you couldn't basically decide from inside that this is how I'm going to play. Or even if you saw the wickets, no one threw the wicket away. It was good deliveries," Iyer added.Despite the heavy defeat, Iyer reminded his teammates that India had won the first two matches and urged them to take confidence from those performances ahead of the series decider."It's important to forget about this one, obviously, analyze what went wrong in terms of bowling and batting. But at the back of the mind it's important that we have also won two games. So a lot of inspiration from that one and see to it that we come with a fresh set of mind," he said.New Zealand had earlier posted 333, powered by Will Young 's 125 off 108 balls. Tim Seifert contributed 58, while Finn Allen scored 41. Henry then led the bowling effort with six wickets as India suffered one of their heaviest defeats in ODI cricket.The fifth and final ODI will be played at the same venue on November 15, with India aiming to secure the series and New Zealand looking to level it.
Article Summary: India's stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer admits New Zealand's bowling made the difference. India were bowled out for 89 in 28.4 overs in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui. The defeat reduced India's lead in the five-match series to 2-1, with the third ODI washed out.

Article Title: Has ‘sanatani’ Akhilesh Yadav finally walked out of ‘Mullah’ Mulayam’s shadows?
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav plans to visit the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, 2026. (File pic: Akhilesh Yadav and Mulayam Singh Yadav)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





LUCKNOW: In the early 1990s, Samajwadi Party founder and the then chief minister Mulayam Singh Yadav was given the moniker ‘Mullah Mulayam’ over his decision to order police firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya at the peak of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple.In the years that followed Mulayam unabashedly went on to don the chequered scarf and dupalli topi at Iftar parties that he organised at party headquarters and his official residence as UP CM to consolidate his then newly formed party among Muslims.Cut to 2026. Mulayam’s son Akhilesh, who is now the SP chief, is set to pay his maiden visit the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, almost three years after the grand Pran Pratishtha (consecration) ceremony of the deity on January 22, 2024. Akhilesh has also initiated the construction of a huge Kedareshwar temple on a sprawling 50 bighas of land in Etawah around 20 kilometres from his native village Saifai.Earlier, he had got a 51-foot, 60-ton bronze and copper statue of Lord Krishna installed at Saifai. He frequently visits temples, attends bhandaras and advocates Sanatan practices. Along with this, the party indulges in extensive and meaningful Muslim outreach with Akhilesh attending dozens of Iftar events every Ramzan, donning his red cap where every precaution is taken to ensure that such engagements do not offer a handle to the political rivals to take on SP for “appeasement of Muslims”.On the face of it, Akhilesh’s strategy to flaunt his bent towards his own faith and at the same time reach out to Muslims aggressively may appear to be more of an election strategy that gains credence in every polls season. However, political experts describe the move as a well-crafted attempt to reflect Akhilesh as the “people’s” leader - a very backbone of the socialist ideology that SP rests on. Experts believe that over the years Akhilesh has done some well-balanced tight-rope-walks to shed the ‘appeasement’ labels that the party had acquired with founder Mulayam Singh at the helm - moves that may have been apt for their times but were not politically viable today.Party insiders say the need for a shift in strategy was underscored after BJP swept one election after another riding the Hindutva wave, starting from 2014 Lok Sabha polls. In 2017 assembly polls that followed, UP got its first saffron-clad chief minister in Yogi Adityanath .While reviewing the factors that went in favour of the BJP in 2017, the SP strategists decided that party leadership following the Hindu religion ardently needed more public mentions because the Yadavs were public figures, it was important for them to share with the people such spiritual moments of their religious side as well. The party made cautious efforts to ensure that Akhilesh’s engagements with Hindu religious affairs like performing Puja at home, attending religious rituals with his wife, were shared publicly.Initial attempts like Akhilesh’s decision to visit a temple to install a statue at a temple in Lucknow in September 2017, faced severe protests from right wing activists. But it did not deter SP chief from visits to Vindhyachal temple in Mirzapur, Ravidas temple in Varanasi’s Seer Goverdhanpur, camp in Chitrakoot where Lord Ram had spent 12 years of his 14-year-exile and staying at the Kamadgiri temple in the years that followed.At the same time, party strategists also made sure that the Yadav family’s religious indulgence remained separate from the party’s political affairs. Instead of religious events being held at party headquarters, Akhilesh went out to different communities himself to take part in their religious events. Apart from Hindu temples, Akhilesh visited Gurudwaras to attend Sikh events, Bengali Club during Durga Puja and Iftar parties during Ramzan.Initial fears of the party that any bold Hindu outreach may leave the Muslim community disenchanted from SP were proved wrong in bypolls on Kairana Lok Sabha seat and Nooorpur assembly seat in 2018. SP was contesting Noorpur and alliance partner RLD was in fray in Kairana. Akhilesh did not address a single rally in either of the constituencies still SP bagged Noorpur and RLD won Kairana – both have sizeable Muslim population.Akhilesh’s absence was deliberate about the premise that RLD will bag Jat votes which are the core constituency of the party. At the same time, the party was confident that Muslims would stand by SP too. With the Bahujan Samaj Party and Congress away from the contest, the calculation was no rocket science. The bypolls were SP’s first step towards shedding its image of being a party that heavily leaned on the support of Muslims after Yadavs.A year later, after the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) was passed in 2019 providing for fast-track processing to claims for Indian citizenship by undocumented non-Muslim and talks of nationwide 2019 NRC led to large scale protest across India, Akhilesh compared the Muslim women protesting at Shaheenbagh in Delhi to Jhansi ki Rani. In Lucknow Muslim women activists like Sumaiya Rana, who led the anti CAA and NRC protests, formally joined SP when the issue was still hot.The fact that Muslims did neither side with BSP or the AIMIM during the 2022 assembly polls or 2024 Lok Sabha elections and voted en masse for SP like never before, stood as an evidence of the fact that the community had become very much aware of how BJP would benefit if SP adopted a ‘visibly’ proactive approach towards Muslims.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav plans to visit the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, 2026. He frequently visits temples, attends bhandaras and advocates Sanatan practices. Akhilesh attends dozens of Iftar events every Ramzan, donning his red cap.

Article Title: Devotional Bhojpuri songs at Mumbai stations trigger row
Article Text:

MUMBAI: Language wars again erupted in Mumbai, this time over the playing of devotional Bhojpuri songs at several Central Railway and Western Railway stations ahead of Chhath Puja Following warnings of agitation from local outfits, which alleged a threat to the state’s Marathi identity, the songs were stopped at some stations.While some passengers urged the authorities to prioritise suburban train punctuality and amenities instead, other commuter outfits said creating such a controversy would only harm Mumbai’s cosmopolitan identity.This is the first time that Bhojpuri songs are being played at stations like CSMT and LTT, where special trains are being run for Chhath Puja.Jitu Patil of Maharashtra Navnirman Railway Sena said, “We warned the administration that if the songs were not stopped in an hour, we would launch an agitation.”Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator Mandhuri Vishwasrao Manjrekar said she was alerted to the issue by passengers from her constituency.“I am not against any language, but regular announcements were compromised because of the songs being played at Wadala station.
